recent_posts.title: Baseline Layered UI Patterns: <dialog> and popover
recent_posts.summary: Native browser APIs for layered UI patterns — the `<dialog>` element and `popover` attribute — offer built-in alternatives to custom JavaScript or third-party libraries for modals, popovers, and similar overlays. The tutorial walks through a practical example of a login-required modal triggered when a user tries to save an image to favorites, covering how to open and close dialogs, autofocus behavior, styling the `::backdrop` pseudo-element, and animating entrance/exit transitions with `@starting-style`.

recent_posts.title: Sass relevance in modern CSS and web design philosophy
recent_posts.summary: A podcast episode featuring Miriam Suzanne discussing the philosophy and evolution of web design, covering CSS origins, the cascade, accessibility, and the balance between user control and brand expression on the web. The conversation touches on whether Sass remains relevant in the modern CSS landscape.

recent_posts.title: Building a simple responsive type scale with modern CSS
recent_posts.summary: A practical look at building a responsive type scale for websites using modern CSS, without needing complex math or equations. Covers different approaches to responsive typography and how CSS features can simplify the process.

recent_posts.title: Container Queries and Units in Action
recent_posts.summary: CSS container queries and container units (like `cqi`) enable components to adapt their layout based on their parent container's size rather than the viewport. By declaring `container-type: inline-size` on elements like `product-list` and `shopping-cart`, you can use `@container` rules as breakpoints that respond to the container's dimensions. This approach is demonstrated through a store layout where a product component must fit into multiple list layouts including a sidebar.

recent_posts.title: Responsive and Fluid Typography with Baseline CSS Features
recent_posts.summary: Fluid typography requires balancing viewport-based sizing with user font preferences. Using CSS comparison functions like clamp() with em/rem and viewport units allows responsive text scaling without forcing a choice between fixed and relative units. The key challenge is ensuring font sizes remain responsive to both available space and user accessibility settings, as viewport-responsive sizing can conflict with user-defined font preferences.

recent_posts.title: CSS IS AWESOME Game 2
recent_posts.summary: The second annual CSS is Awesome Game features a competitive challenge between CSS professionals Adam Argyle, Cassondra Roberts, Dave Rupert, and Miriam Suzanne. The episode is part of the Winging It podcast series, which regularly discusses CSS features, design systems, and web development topics with industry experts.

recent_posts.title: Remove polish from early design mockups to focus client feedback
recent_posts.summary: High-fidelity design mockups can mislead clients into focusing on superficial details like colors and fonts rather than core structural decisions. OddBird deliberately removes polish from early mockups using techniques like grayscale filters, off-brand fonts, or scribbled annotations to help clients understand what stage the design is in and provide appropriate feedback. This approach prevents 'premature sheen' from creating false impressions of completeness and keeps conversations focused on the right questions at each phase of the project.

recent_posts.title: Cross-Browser Anchor Positioning
recent_posts.summary: CSS Anchor Positioning has achieved cross-browser support across all major browsers. The discussion explores what comes next for this positioning feature with Eric Meyer, examining its implications for web layout and design patterns.

recent_posts.title: Anchor Positioning Updates for Fall 2025
recent_posts.summary: CSS anchor positioning is approaching Baseline status with Safari 26 support joining Chrome, while Firefox implementation is in progress. Current browser implementations show differences in handling overflow behavior and position-try-fallback, with the CSSWG working on standardization. Upcoming changes include adjustments to popover UA styles, position-area syntax modifications, transform support, and anchored container queries. The CSS Anchor Positioning Polyfill v0.7.0 now supports shadow DOM elements.

recent_posts.title: Combining CSS units for better responsive design
recent_posts.summary: CSS units like px, rem, and em each serve different purposes and can be combined using functions like clamp(), max(), and calc() to create more flexible designs. Rather than choosing one unit type, developers can express design intent more clearly by combining units that represent different relationships - using rem for consistency across pages, em for local context, and px for fixed values. This approach allows for better negotiation between user preferences and design requirements, particularly for typography and spacing.
